subject: PayFlux incident: recommended short-term mitigation and deployment path options
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@payflux.com>; PayFlux SRE <sre@payflux.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary + urgent next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Daniel / PayFlux team,

Thanks again for the call today — appreciate you walking us through the outage window and the traffic spike details. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move fast:

1) What we heard
- Recent production spike caused a ~15% elevation in 5xxs across inference endpoints during your nightly batch window.
- Current steady-state: ~2.5M tokens/day; peak bursts up to ~400 reqs/min for 8–10 minutes.
- Must-have constraints: data residency for transaction traces; procurement needs SOC2 evidence and KMS for keys.

2) Immediate ask from our side
- Can you attach the incident SLI window (error rates + traces) and the operational runbook you used during the spike?
- Confirm if traffic spikes are predictable (cron) vs. user-driven.

3) Options we recommend and rough timelines
- Short-term Hosted mitigations (minutes → hours): aggressive prefix caching + temporary quota bump + request routing to a lower-latency region.
- Mid-term Dedicated capacity (24–72 hours if capacity available): predictable throughput, isolation, and easier traffic shaping.
- Private VPC/on-prem (3–6+ weeks): required if procurement insists on full network isolation and HSM-backed keys.

4) Proposed immediate next step
- Stand-up a 30-minute triage call tomorrow 9am PT to lock mitigation steps and confirm whether you want us to provision a Dedicated trial.

I've attached a one-page SLO checklist (payflux_slo_checklist.pdf) and will loop in engineering to size a Dedicated pool if you want to explore that fast.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0157

Attachments: payflux_slo_checklist.pdf

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@payflux.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: PayFlux SRE <sre@payflux.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary + urgent next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Laura. Quick answers — we'll pull detailed logs and share the SLI window in your portal, but high level:

- The spike was caused by a batch reconciliation job that started running concurrently with a client sync; it was semi-predictable (daily, but variable size).
- Error spike: ~15% elevated 5xx for 9 minutes; CPU/GPU queues hit saturation on the shared hosts.
- Current throughput numbers look like what you noted (2.3–2.6M tokens/day).

Immediate constraints from procurement/security:
- We need SOC2 evidence and confirmation on KMS integration. If Dedicated doesn't solve the KMS requirement, our lawyers will push for VPC.
- Timeline: procurement wants a solution in the next 7–10 business days or we risk pausing a subset of our rollout.

Preferably we'd like to move to Dedicated if that gives us isolation and guarantees — but if KMS/HSM access and network isolation are still blockers, we'll need Private.

I'll upload the incident window to the shared folder and loop procurement on the triage call.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho
Director, Platform Engineering — PayFlux
daniel.cho@payflux.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Daniel — PayFlux incident details (need sizing + options)

Vivek / Neha — forwarding Daniel's note. Can you quickly run a sizing/ops note and confirm:
- 24/48/72 hour path to Dedicated (what's blocking vs capacity we can offer)
- Required steps for KMS + SOC2 evidence handoff (fast path vs Private availability)
- Any short-term Hosted mitigations we can apply today that don't require an infra change (rate-limit, cache TTLs, routing)

If Dedicated can be stood up in 48 hours with a TTL-limited trial, let's prepare a concise MAP for PayFlux and pricing (they're pushing procurement).

Thanks — laura

> Thanks Laura. Quick answers — we'll pull detailed logs and share the SLI window in your portal, but high level:
> ...

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Daniel — PayFlux incident details (need sizing + options)

Laura / Neha — quick technical read:

1) Short-term Hosted mitigations (minutes → hours)\- We can apply:
  - aggressive prefix / KV caching for the batch job paths (should drop token compute by ~30–40% for that workload)
  - per-tenant throttling during the batch window (soft limit + queuing)
  - temporary quota bump on hosted pool (depends on available capacity in the region, estimate: +20% for 72 hours)

2) Dedicated sizing (24–72 hours realistic if capacity available)\- For their peak (400 reqs/min, bursts up to 12 minutes): recommend a pool with 4x A100-equivalent slices (or 6x T4-equivalent depending on model). This gives headroom for the nightly batch and preserves latency SLO.
- Lead time: if we have free slots, provisioning + routing changes = ~24–48 hours; if we need to ship new hardware, 72+ hours.

3) Private VPC/on-prem (3–6 weeks)\- KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed networking are the blockers; security + legal signoffs add time. Not an immediate option for their 7–10 day procurement window.

Attached a quick capacity sketch (dedicated_capacity_plan.xlsx). If sales wants to offer a short Dedicated trial, we should also prepare a fall-back policy (auto-route to hosted with lower concurrency) and an SLA caveat for that trial.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_plan.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@payflux.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>; procurement@payflux.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call summary + urgent next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Daniel / team — thanks for the quick context and Vivek for the sizing. Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) below — attached as a one-pager (MAP_PayFlux_July10.pdf):

1) Immediate (today → 24h):
- Apply prefix caching and tenant throttling for nightly batch window (ops action; expected reduction 25–40%).
- Temporary Hosted quota bump + monitoring for 72 hours while we validate the caching effect.

2) Short window (24–72h):
- Provision a Dedicated trial pool sized per Vivek's recommendation (4x A100-equivalent slices).
- Trial terms: 7-day trail with a pre-agreed escalation path and option to convert to reserved capacity.

3) Procurement/security asks (parallel):
- We'll provide SOC2 evidence (attestation PDF) and initial KMS integration doc within 48 hours.
- If PayFlux requires HSM-backed keys or strict VPC-only traffic, Private onboarding is available but would take 3–6 weeks.

Next steps:
- Can procurement join a 30-min call tomorrow 9am PT to confirm trial commercial terms?
- If you approve the trial, we'll trigger capacity provisioning immediately (we'll need a PO or signed trial agreement).

I'll prepare a short commercial MAP and pricing sheet right after this and send the DocuSign link for an expedited trial agreement.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0157

2) SOC2 evidence + a short KMS integration runbook (how keys are managed and whether we can use our own KMS/HSM).
